entry.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
entry.summary:
AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #rust

entry.title: flodl-bio: First Rust data, transformers and model layer for entire deep learning on biological sequences
entry.summary:
Python ecosystem dominates the deep learning framework. flodl-bio is a Rust crate that extends flodl, a libtorch-backed deep-learning framework, with deep learning on biological sequences. To our knowledge, flodl-bio is the first Rust crate that provides a comprehensive and practical deep learning for the biological applications, which includes the alphabet-aware sequence encoding, including one-hot and k-mer representations, padded sequences, and channels-first batches.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9 The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

entry.title: On "AI Brendans" or "Virtual Brendans". There are now multiple AI performance engineering agents that use or are trained on my work.
entry.summary:
There are now multiple AI performance engineering agents that use or are trained on my work. Some are helper agents that interpret flame graphs or eBPF metrics, sometimes privately called AI Brendan ; others have trained on my work to create a virtual Brendan that claims it can tune everything just like the real thing. These virtual Brendans sound like my brain has been uploaded to the cloud by someone who is now selling it (yikes!).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #rust #distributed-systems
